script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sports
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. APARTMENT - NIGHT

JAMES (30s, disheveled, desperate), sits on his couch, staring at the blank TV screen. He clenches his jaw, frustrated. He has just lost his job as a professional soccer player due to an injury.

JAMES
(whispering to himself)
I can't believe this is happening to me. After all the hard work, all the training, it's over.

The doorbell rings. James hesitates, then gets up, hobbling to the door.

INT. APARTMENT ENTRANCE - NIGHT

James opens the door to reveal OLIVER (40s, calm, confident), a former professional basketball player, now a successful businessman.

OLIVER
(smiling)
Hey, James. I heard about your injury. I'm really sorry to hear that.

JAMES
(sighs)
Thanks, Oliver. I'm just trying to figure out what to do next.

OLIVER
(pauses)
Well, have you considered coaching?

JAMES
(scoffs)
Coaching? That's not the same thing as playing.

OLIVER
(nods)
It's not the same, but it can be just as rewarding. And you have a unique perspective that many coaches lack - you've been in the shoes of the players you'll be coaching.

James considers this for a moment.

JAMES
(sighs)
I guess it's worth looking into.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

James and Oliver sit at a table, laptops open, researching soccer coaching opportunities.

OLIVER
(looking at an article)
Here's an article about a former soccer player who became a successful coach. Maybe this will give you some ideas.

James scans the article, his eyes widening as he reads about the ex-player's accomplishments.

JAMES
(excited)
Wow, this is really inspiring. I can do this.

OLIVER
(smiling)
Of course you can. Now, let's start looking for openings.

INT. SOCCER CLUB - DAY

James and Oliver sit in front of the soccer club's director, HANNAH (30s, stern, no-nonsense).

HANNAH
(skeptical)
And why should we hire you, James? You have no coaching experience.

JAMES
(confident)
But I have extensive playing experience, and I've been mentored by a successful businessman, Oliver, who has given me the tools and confidence to succeed as a coach.

HANNAH
(pauses)
Alright, we'll give you a trial run. You'll start coaching our U-10 team.

JAMES
(elated)
Thank you, Hannah. I won't let you down.

INT. SOCCER FIELD - DAY

James stands in front of his new team, nervously clutching a whistle. The kids watch him curiously.

JAMES
(clears throat)
Alright, team, let's get started.

The team giggles and chatter, but James manages to gain their attention and begins to coach them.

INT. APARTMENT - NIGHT

James sits on his couch, surrounded by papers and soccer equipment. He looks exhausted but satisfied.

JAMES
(to himself)
I'm doing it. I'm a coach.

The phone rings, and James answers it to hear Oliver's voice.

OLIVER
(proud)
I'm so proud of you, James. You've taken a difficult situation and turned it into an opportunity.

JAMES
(smiling)
Thanks, Oliver. I couldn't have done it without you.

FADE OUT.

THE END
